case_title: Krishan Kumar Malik v. State of Haryana
evidence_type: Solitary oral testimony of the prosecutrix; medical evidence of PW-6; FIR and s.164/s.161 CrPC statements; semen-stained undergarments not forensically analysed
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.366 IPC and s.376(2)(g) IPC; ten years R.I. and Rs. 2000 fine under s.376(2)(g), and five years R.I. with Rs. 1000 fine under s.366 IPC
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed; two co-accused acquitted; conviction of the appellant under ss.366 and 376(2)(g) IPC upheld
neutral_facts: The victim, a seventeen-year-old woman, went with her younger sister to meet her aunt at the aunt's house. While they were talking, a group of persons including the accused arrived at the house, and the victim was forcibly lifted into a blue Maruti van despite raised alarm by the aunt, her husband and neighbours. The victim was taken to a vacant building near a bridge and placed in a separate room, where two men were said to have sexually assaulted her while others fondled her body; one was said to have inserted a finger into her anus and another bit her cheek. The victim was later taken in the same van to another house, where she was beaten, and she then escaped by bus to meet her mother and sister, to whom she narrated the incident. An FIR was recorded the following night. The FIR described one man as short-statured with a beard and did not name the accused. Medical examination found no injuries to the labia, an old healed hymen tear, and no significant injuries apart from a cheek bite. Statements were recorded under sections 164 and 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Male semen was found in the victim's undergarments but was not sent for forensic analysis. No spot map was prepared, the investigating officer did not visit the spot, and the victim could not identify the building when taken to the area. No identification parade was held, and the victim had seen the accused at the police station before identifying him in court. The aunt, her husband, their sons, neighbours, the victim's mother and sister were not examined.
physical_harm: Minor: cheek bite; no significant injuries on other body parts; old healed hymen tear; labia healthy with no marks of injury
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence was relied on to convict. The Court accepted the medical findings (healthy labia, old healed hymen tear, no significant injuries) and the failure to forensically test the semen as weakening the case.
witness_credibility: The Court found the prosecutrix not credible: she did not name the appellant in the FIR, varied the number of assailants, was shown to be a member of a musical concert party despite denying it, failed to identify the building, and her account of meeting her mother and sister was held concocted.
trial_duration: offence: 23.06.1994; trial judgment: 24.04.1996; High Court: 27.03.2009; Supreme Court: 04.07.2011
legal_representation: Appellant: Jaspal Singh (Senior Advocate), Sanjeev Anand, Yakesh Anand, Nimit Mathur, Vikram Anand. State: Roopansh Purohit, Ramesh Kumar (for Kamal Mohan Gupta)
investigation_status: FIR registered 24.06.1994; medical examination done; s.164 and s.161 statements recorded; accused arrested; trial held (charge sheet not separately described)
procedural_irregularity: No identification parade; no spot map prepared; investigating officer never visited the spot; aunt, her family, neighbours, mother and sister not examined; semen not sent for forensic analysis; s.164 statement recorded before s.161 statement; victim shown accused at police station before dock identification
appeal_history: Trial court: all eight convicted under s.366; four including appellant convicted under s.376(2)(g). High Court: two acquitted, appellant's conviction upheld. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, appellant acquitted
prosecution_argument: Respondent-State's counsel drew attention to s.53A CrPC on DNA testing; no other prosecution submissions are recorded in the judgment
defence_argument: Appellant's counsel stated, after verification from the appellant's wife, that he is 5'6" tall, not the short-statured man described; the description did not match; dock identification was meaningless
legal_principle_applied: A solitary prosecutrix's testimony can convict only if it inspires confidence, is trustworthy, unblemished and of sterling quality; lacunae in investigation benefit the accused; s.6 Evidence Act res gestae requires statements made contemporaneously with the act
precedent_relied_upon: None cited; the Court relied on Taylor's Principles and Practice of Medical Jurisprudence and Black's Law Dictionary (texts, not precedents)
other_sentence_order: Appellant to be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other criminal case
